Owner

Closes #161 and #169. The marker — syntax, recognition and display — is specification §3.6, delivered by #160. This pull request makes the review skills write it (#161), and lifts the last-line condition that footer-signing publishers could not meet (#169), in one change as the maintainer chose.

Recognition anywhere, display at the bottom (#169)

Core (@cct/core)

  • [session:<value>] is recognized on any line where it stands alone — last, middle, before a signature footer, above the prefix line — still not inline, in fenced code or in a quotation, nor with an empty value or another form.
  • Every marker line is removed from the body with its line ending before §3.4.1 preprocessing; a marker above the prefix line leaves the same verdict as one at the bottom.
  • Two or more markers designate no session and raise W-SESSION-MULTIPLE, a warning (never blocks, even under enforce), ordered after the content checks, due whether or not the prefix is recognized, absent from exempt or excluded comments.

Extension

  • Each marker line is hidden where it stands, without a trace: a paragraph reduced to the marker is hidden whole (class cct-hidden-session-block on the platform's paragraph, removed on undo), a line inside a paragraph is wrapped with the break that ends it.
  • One mention is placed at the bottom of the body, below a footer: 🤖 session: <lowercased value>, or 🤖 session: #ERROR with the diagnostic as its title when there are several markers.
  • The subject wrapper, its spacer and the tightened header margin skip hidden marker lines; all-or-nothing fallback when any line cannot be found safely in the rendered DOM.
  • check:session-line now measures in Chromium that a marker mid-body, mid-paragraph, above the prefix (own paragraph or same paragraph) and duplicated lays out exactly like the same comment with the marker at the bottom, and that the mention sits one paragraph gap below a footer. Removing the line-break hiding makes it fail with the 21 px empty line it guards against.

Specification: §3.5.2 (new W-SESSION-MULTIPLE row), §3.6 (position, one marker per comment, marker above the prefix), §5.5 (hidden in place, mention at the bottom, #ERROR, no trace, all-or-nothing fallback), CA-51 and CA-53 amended, CA-54 added; docs/ca-matrix-fr.md follows.

Review skills (#161)

Reviewer (skills/review-pull-request/)

  • Section 9, Session marker: one identifier per review session, chosen once and reused on every pass, on its own line in every comment of the session — findings, recaps, follow-ups and the final reviewed: — last when possible, a footer after it being fine; once per comment.
  • How the identifier is drawn is settled once per installation, through session-id-setup.md:
    1. if Slugger already runs — local tool manifest (dotnet slugger) or global install (slugger) — use it without asking, with the command that answered, and only offer to record the choice;
    2. otherwise offer Slugger to the person the agent works for (never on the pull request), copy the chosen option verbatim into session-id.md beside the loaded SKILL.md, add Slugger.Cli to the local tool manifest when chosen, and commit that on its own, never in the pull request under review.
    • Slugger declined → a GUID, by the person's explicit choice. No answer, or Slugger chosen but unable to run → a readable kebab-case identifier made up in the theme's style; a GUID only as a last resort.
  • Slugger's code-review theme ships with the skill (code-review.json, Apache-2.0, see THIRD-PARTY.md and code-review.LICENSE), read in place through --theme-dir.

Author (skills/respond-to-review/SKILL.md): a reply copies the marker of the comment it answers, thread by thread, once; none when that comment has none; never a self-drawn identifier.

This repository chooses Slugger: dotnet-tools.json pins Slugger.Cli 1.0.0, .claude/skills/review-pull-request/session-id.md sits beside the Claude Code pointer. README: the skills are directories, to install or hand over whole.

Verification

  • npm test: 1659 passed (37 skipped, as on main); npm run checks and typecheck:tests pass.
  • In Chromium: check:session-line (19 measures), check:subject-line, check:composer-layout, check:style-isolation, smoke:mv3 pass.
  • check:pr-scope: shared code only.
  • With the .NET 10 SDK, dotnet slugger --theme-dir skills/review-pull-request --theme code-review --oneshot draws names such as tedious-debated-branch.

Known limits

  • An installation that chose Slugger makes up a readable name on a machine without the .NET SDK.
  • The theme copy stays at 1.0.1 until updated by hand.
  • The duplicate's explanation shows in the composer with the other diagnostics, and as the mention's title on published comments; exempt and excluded comments get the #ERROR mention without a diagnostic, since they are not judged.

f1e101a 
Owner decision: pull request descriptions carry no Claude Code footer.
A CLAUDE.md rule cannot achieve it: on #167 the session sent a body
without a footer and the pull request creation tool added one. Editing
a description through the tool adds nothing (measured on #165), so the
footer is removed after creation, by a workflow the tool never touches.

The workflow runs on pull_request_target (the only trigger whose token
may write to a fork's pull request) and never checks out the pull
request's code: it reads the description, strips a trailing footer in
either known form, and writes it back. Edits made with GITHUB_TOKEN
trigger no workflow, so it cannot loop.

Since #169 the marker is recognized on any line where it stands alone,
so a marker followed by the footer is no longer unrecognized. The
footer-stripping test asserted the old last-line rule; it now checks
that the core recognizes the marker with and without the footer, and

5ea8da2 
Review of #165. §3.6 promises that a duplicate session marker never
blocks sending, but `severities` could promote W-SESSION-MULTIPLE to
`error`, at repository or floor level, making the comment non-compliant
under enforce. Configuration resolution now lowers such a value to
`warn` with a config warning, and finalizeDiagnostics caps it as a
defence in depth; `off` stays allowed. §8.2 states the upper limit,
§3.6 and CA-54 refer to it.
